title: First Thing: Mississippi turns blue as Scott Colom unseats Republican Senate incumbent
summary: Defeating Cindy Hyde-Smith makes the 43-year-old district attorney the first Black Mississippi senator elected since Reconstruction. Plus, the South Korean scarf vendor who has gone viral for…

blocks.text: Good morning. In a stunning upset after more than a week of vote counting in one of the country’s most reliably red states, the Democrat Scott Colom has defeated Cindy Hyde-Smith, the incumbent Republican senator, in Mississippi. He becomes the first Black senator elected in the state since Reconstruction.

Colom’s election capped a national wave of anger at Donald Trump’s administration, sweeping away Republicans in places where Democrats had not been competitive in decades. With the addition of Colom, Democrats will hold at least 55 seats in the Senate, the party’s largest midterm gain since 1986.

items: What did Colom say about his victory? Colom, a 43-year-old district attorney, said there had been times when his long-shot campaign felt defeated but “I had to have faith”. He told supporters: “My commitment to you, each and every one of you, is that first I’m going to treat your children like I want my children to be treated. I’m going to treat your parents the way I want my parents to be treated. I’m gonna treat your future the way I want my future to be.”

How have Democrats responded to a White House threat? Robert Garcia, the ranking member of the oversight committee in the House of Representatives said it appeared Donald Trump had “something to hide” after the White House threatened criminal investigations over the party’s planned scrutiny of the administration. Garcia said in a statement that Congress’s authority came from article I of the constitution, “not from the permission of the White House”.

blocks.text: Nvidia board reportedly deciding whether to oust CEO Jensen Huang as stock price plunges

Nvidia’s board of directors has met to decide whether to oust Jensen Huang as CEO of the world’s most valuable chip company, according to reports, after a tumultuous week in which the executive and co-founder of the company admitted to having a romantic relationship with a woman who is alleged to be a Chinese spy. Huang’s position became more tenuous late on Wednesday after it was reported by the New York Times that Huang had a separate extramarital affair with a company employee. Our global technology editor, Dan Milmo, explains what is happening in our Today in Focus podcast.
Democrats lambast absent peers after Republicans block Hegseth impeachment attempt

blocks.caption: From left: Nancy Pelosi, Steven Horsford and Haley Stevens, who all failed to vote. Composite: Getty Images, Bloomberg

blocks.text: Democratic lawmakers expressed outrage at nearly a dozen of their colleagues for missing a vote Tuesday evening to impeach the defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, allowing Republicans to defeat the effort. Eleven Democrats missed the key procedural vote on the impeachment effort, which failed by just seven votes. “You should show up and do your job,” Abdul El-Sayed, the senator-elect of Michigan, said on CNN, while Richard Ojeda, the representative-elect of North Carolina, said: “Shame on them for not showing up … they had an opportunity to finally get rid of this buffoonery.”

items: Why has a video clip of Hegseth gone viral? A US army sentinel guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier loudly reprimanded the defense secretary and his top staffers on Wednesday after some in the group were heard laughing and talking near the memorial following a Veterans Day ceremony. You can watch the video here.

blocks.text: Brooklyn building collapse kills at least eight people and traps others in wreckage

blocks.caption: Emergency personnel work at the scene of the building collapse. Photograph: Angelina Katsanis/Reuters

blocks.text: Firefighters dug through the rubble of a three-story building in Brooklyn on Wednesday after it collapsed at the edge of a construction site, killing at least eight people and trapping others beneath the wreckage. Firefighters were called to the scene in the borough’s Flatbush section at about 4pm.

items: Russia’s ambassador to the United States has died aged 66. Alexander Darchiev took up the role last year.
The US could lose its measles elimination status under RFK Jr’s leadership, with the country in the middle of worst measles outbreak since 1991.
Average US heating bills are set to rise 7% this winter, according a report by the National Energy Assistance Directors Association.

Starbucks baristas, students, elected officials and allies are holding rallies at more than 40 college campuses across the US to support the Starbucks Workers United boycott campaign as the union nears five years of deadlock with the company over contract negotiations.
Two skulls that likely belonged to enslaved people are being returned to Brazil after Harvard used them in eugenics studies. The remains had been outside Brazil since the 19th century.
A coyote that officials thought they had killed after it attacked a child has been seen alive in an LA neighborhood.

blocks.text: Last Thing: ‘He’s the hottest thing right now’ – how a $1 scarf seller became Seoul’s biggest attraction

blocks.caption: People ask private security personnel about the store’s operating hours. Photograph: SuhJeen Moon/SuhJeen Moon for The Guardian

blocks.text: Seoul’s “scarf uncle” has become a South Korean sensation for a sales technique that consists of talking customers out of purchases. The combination of his affectionate bluntness and amusing selling style – coupled with praise for his looks – has led to him becoming a huge star on social media.
